L16: ## 6.29 Limits and colimits of sheaves
L17: 
L18: Let $X$ be a topological space. Let $\mathcal{I} \to \mathop{\mathit{Sh}}\nolimits (X)$, $i \mapsto \mathcal{F}_ i$ be a diagram.
L19: 
L20:   1. Both $\mathop{\mathrm{lim}}\nolimits _ i \mathcal{F}_ i$ and $\mathop{\mathrm{colim}}\nolimits _ i \mathcal{F}_ i$ exist.
L21:   2. The inclusion functor $i : \mathop{\mathit{Sh}}\nolimits (X) \to \textit{PSh}(X)$ commutes with limits. In other words, we may compute the limit in the category of sheaves as the limit in the category of presheaves. In particular, for any open $U \subset X$ we have
L22: 
L23: \[ (\mathop{\mathrm{lim}}\nolimits _ i \mathcal{F}_ i)(U) = \mathop{\mathrm{lim}}\nolimits _ i \mathcal{F}_ i(U). \]
L24:   3. The inclusion functor $i : \mathop{\mathit{Sh}}\nolimits (X) \to \textit{PSh}(X)$ does not commute with colimits in general (not even with finite colimits – think surjections). The colimit is computed as the sheafification of the colimit in the category of presheaves:
L25: 
L26: \[ \mathop{\mathrm{colim}}\nolimits _ i \mathcal{F}_ i = \Big(U \mapsto \mathop{\mathrm{colim}}\nolimits _ i \mathcal{F}_ i(U)\Big)^\# . \]
L27:   4. Let $x \in X$ be a point. In general the stalk of $\mathop{\mathrm{lim}}\nolimits _ i \mathcal{F}_ i$ at $x$ is not equal to the limit of the stalks. But if the index category is finite then it is the case. In other words, the stalk functor is left exact.
L28: 
L29:   5. Let $x \in X$. We always have
L30: 
L31: \[ (\mathop{\mathrm{colim}}\nolimits _ i \mathcal{F}_ i)_ x = \mathop{\mathrm{colim}}\nolimits _ i \mathcal{F}_{i, x}. \]
L32:   6. The sheafification functor ${}^\# : \textit{PSh}(X) \to \mathop{\mathit{Sh}}\nolimits (X)$ commutes with all colimits, and with finite limits. But it does not commute with all limits.
L33: 
L34: The proofs are all easy. Here is an example of what is true for directed colimits of sheaves.
L35: 【11†Lemma 6.29.1.】 Let $X$ be a topological space. Let $I$ be a directed set. Let $(\mathcal{F}_ i, \varphi _{ii'})$ be a system of sheaves of sets over $I$, see Categories, Section 【12†4.21】. Let $U \subset X$ be an open subset. Consider the canonical map
L36: 
L37: \[ \Psi : \mathop{\mathrm{colim}}\nolimits _ i \mathcal{F}_ i(U) \longrightarrow \left(\mathop{\mathrm{colim}}\nolimits _ i \mathcal{F}_ i\right)(U) \]
L38: 
L39:   1. If all the transition maps are injective then $\Psi $ is injective for any open $U$.
L40:   2. If $U$ is quasi-compact, then $\Psi $ is injective.
L41: 
L42:   3. If $U$ is quasi-compact and all the transition maps are injective then $\Psi $ is an isomorphism.
L43: 
L44:   4. If $U$ has a cofinal system of open coverings $\mathcal{U} : U = \bigcup _{j\in J} U_ j$ with $J$ finite and $U_ j \cap U_{j'}$ quasi-compact for all $j, j' \in J$, then $\Psi $ is bijective.
L45: Proof. Assume all the transition maps are injective. In this case the presheaf $\mathcal{F}' : V \mapsto \mathop{\mathrm{colim}}\nolimits _ i \mathcal{F}_ i(V)$ is separated (see Definition 【13†6.11.2】). By the discussion above we have $(\mathcal{F}')^\# = \mathop{\mathrm{colim}}\nolimits _ i \mathcal{F}_ i$. By Lemma 【14†6.17.5】 we see that $\mathcal{F}' \to (\mathcal{F}')^\# $ is injective. This proves (1).
L46: Assume $U$ is quasi-compact. Suppose that $s \in \mathcal{F}_ i(U)$ and $s' \in \mathcal{F}_{i'}(U)$ give rise to elements on the left hand side which have the same image under $\Psi $. Since $U$ is quasi-compact this means there exists a finite open covering $U = \bigcup _{j = 1, \ldots , m} U_ j$ and for each $j$ an index $i_ j \in I$, $i_ j \geq i$, $i_ j \geq i'$ such that $\varphi _{ii_ j}(s)$ and $\varphi _{i'i_ j}(s')$ have the same restriction to $U_ j$.

L23: 【8†Lemma 17.3.3.】 Let $f : (X, \mathcal{O}_ X) \to (Y, \mathcal{O}_ Y)$ be a morphism of ringed spaces.
L24: 
L25:   1. The functor $f_* : \textit{Mod}(\mathcal{O}_ X) \to \textit{Mod}(\mathcal{O}_ Y)$ is left exact. In fact it commutes with all limits.
L26: 
L27:   2. The functor $f^* : \textit{Mod}(\mathcal{O}_ Y) \to \textit{Mod}(\mathcal{O}_ X)$ is right exact. In fact it commutes with all colimits.
L28: 
L29:   3. Pullback $f^{-1} : \textit{Ab}(Y) \to \textit{Ab}(X)$ on abelian sheaves is exact.
L30: Proof. Parts (1) and (2) hold because $(f^*, f_*)$ is an adjoint pair of functors, see Sheaves, Lemma 【15†6.26.2】 and Categories, Section 【16†4.24】. Part (3) holds because exactness can be checked on stalks (Lemma 【17†17.3.1】) and the description of stalks of the pullback, see Sheaves, Lemma 【18†6.22.1】. $\square$

L16: ## 10.63 Associated primes
L17: 
L18: Here is the standard definition. For non-Noetherian rings and non-finite modules it may be more appropriate to use the definition in Section 【11†10.66】.
L19: 
L20: 【12†Definition 10.63.1.】 Let $R$ be a ring. Let $M$ be an $R$-module. A prime $\mathfrak p$ of $R$ is associated to $M$ if there exists an element $m \in M$ whose annihilator is $\mathfrak p$. The set of all such primes is denoted $\text{Ass}_ R(M)$ or $\text{Ass}(M)$.
L21: 【13†Lemma 10.63.2.】 Let $R$ be a ring. Let $M$ be an $R$-module. Then $\text{Ass}(M) \subset \text{Supp}(M)$.
L22: 
L23: Proof. If $m \in M$ has annihilator $\mathfrak p$, then in particular no element of $R \setminus \mathfrak p$ annihilates $m$. Hence $m$ is a nonzero element of $M_{\mathfrak p}$, i.e., $\mathfrak p \in \text{Supp}(M)$. $\square$
L24: 【14†Lemma 10.63.3.】 Let $R$ be a ring. Let $0 \to M' \to M \to M'' \to 0$ be a short exact sequence of $R$-modules. Then $\text{Ass}(M') \subset \text{Ass}(M)$ and $\text{Ass}(M) \subset \text{Ass}(M') \cup \text{Ass}(M'')$. Also $\text{Ass}(M' \oplus M'') = \text{Ass}(M') \cup \text{Ass}(M'')$.
L25: Proof. If $m' \in M'$, then the annihilator of $m'$ viewed as an element of $M'$ is the same as the annihilator of $m'$ viewed as an element of $M$. Hence the inclusion $\text{Ass}(M') \subset \text{Ass}(M)$. Let $m \in M$ be an element whose annihilator is a prime ideal $\mathfrak p$. If there exists a $g \in R$, $g \not\in \mathfrak p$ such that $m' = gm \in M'$ then the annihilator of $m'$ is $\mathfrak p$.
L26: If there does not exist a $g \in R$, $g \not\in \mathfrak p$ such that $gm \in M'$, then the annilator of the image $m'' \in M''$ of $m$ is $\mathfrak p$. This proves the inclusion $\text{Ass}(M) \subset \text{Ass}(M') \cup \text{Ass}(M'')$. We omit the proof of the final statement. $\square$
L27: 【15†Lemma 10.63.4.】 Let $R$ be a ring, and $M$ an $R$-module. Suppose there exists a filtration by $R$-submodules
L28: 
L29: \[ 0 = M_0 \subset M_1 \subset \ldots \subset M_ n = M \]
L30:
